title: Redwood All-Hands - August 2026
summary: Monthly company all-hands: product updates (Optimize, Dedicated, Private), Q2 metrics recap, hiring and org changes, security/compliance update, roadmap highlights, and open Q&A. Several action items to follow: publish benchmark report, schedule product AMA, finalize hiring plan for infra team.
transcript:
[00:00] Miguel Torres: Good morning, everyone, welcome to the August all hands. Uh, I think we're at the top of the hour, so we'll get started. Thanks for making time. Quick note, we are recording, and the deck is up in the #all-hands channel.

[00:18] Ava Chen: Hey team, quick run through the agenda — metrics, product, security, people, then Q&A. Tom's gonna walk finances, Priya on product.

[00:34] Tom Beck: Thanks Ava. Quick numbers — revenue growth was up 21% q/q, ARR is now at 44M, churn stayed under 1%. We saw a noticeable uptick in Dedicated signups after the June pricing tweak. Cost per inference improvements landed us about 8% better gross margin on hosted. Uh, caveat there, some of that is seasonal usage.

[01:05] Priya Kapoor: Product — two short updates. First, Redwood Optimize: the rollout of auto-suggest quantization profiles is in limited beta with three customers; initial run shows avg token cost down 18% while latency impact is negligible. We did have one case where model quality regressed on a scoring prompt, we rolled back profile, and it's now in the eval suite.

[01:36] Ethan Li: Right, and on the research side we landed a new kernel selection heuristic that reduces warm-start latency for long-context models — real world traffic saw 5-12% latency improvement depending on sequence length distribution. There's still some polish; the heuristic can mis-pick on very bursty traffic.

[02:00] Janelle Park: On Dedicated and Private: we've shipped the self-service onboarding flow for Dedicated pools, customers can now reserve GPU pools and set autoscale policies without SE assistance. Private (VPC) deployments — we have two pilots in staging, one with a regulated financial customer in EMEA. Note: that pilot required HSM integration for KMS which took longer than expected.

[02:28] Miguel Torres: Big shout out to the infra and SE teams, that HSM work is critical for our Private motion. Also, security/compliance — Samir?

[02:38] Samir Rao: Yep. SOC2 refresh in progress, external audit scheduled for mid-September. We've updated our audit log retention and added more granularity to token-level cost traces. SSO improvements: SAML certificates rotation is now documented in the private console guide. A small transcript note — sometimes the doc references "kay-v cache" in user notes; that's KV cache, just FYI.

[03:05] Audience (someone): There's a question about data residency — are we supporting EU-only data flows for Private?

[03:12] Priya Kapoor: Short answer: yes, via Private and dedicated regional routing we can pin control plane and inference in EU regions, we just need legal to sign off on contract addendum for data processing. Tom, can you add the addendum template to the repo?

[03:28] Tom Beck: Yep I'll follow up.

[03:35] Miguel Torres: Hiring — we are prioritizing infra and SE hiring this quarter. We have approval to open 10 new IC roles across serving runtime, infra reliability, and two senior SEs for enterprise onboarding. Priya: how are we structuring the interviews for the infra roles?

[03:55] Priya Kapoor: We're moving to a two-stage loop: technical deep-dive with an infra engineer and system design with a cross-functional panel. Also adding a short take-home on perf tuning. The goal is to close first offers by end of September.

[04:14] Ethan Li: A note on roadmap: short-term focus is on inference quality monitoring and auto-rollbacks in Optimize, mid-term is model variant routing and multi-tenant KV cache improvements. We demoed a prototype for automatic fallback to lower-cost variants when the primary model hits capacity. It works but needs more safety checks.

[04:45] Audience (someone): Will that fallback affect prompts that rely on deterministic output?

[04:50] Priya Kapoor: Good question. We'll have per-route policies where customers can opt out of automatic fallback for routes that require strict determinism.

[05:03] Miguel Torres: Okay, open Q&A. Please use the raise-hand or post in Slack for follow-ups. We'll do a rapid-fire session.

[05:14] Attendee (Maya): Congrats on the Optimize numbers. Is the eval suite open-source?

[05:20] Ethan Li: Not open-source; it's internal but we share benchmark summaries and prompt sets as redacted examples. We're exploring a community dataset for standard evals but there's IP concerns.

[05:36] Attendee (Ben): Any updates on marketplace partnerships?

[05:40] Miguel Torres: Yes, we have a pilot with a cloud partner for a marketplace listing, expected in Q4. That should help APAC reach.

[05:50] Attendee (Sophie): How do we measure customer success for Dedicated? Metrics?

[05:56] Samir Rao: We track time-to-first-successful-batch, reserved utilization, and SLO attainment per pool. Also NPS for the onboarding flow. Early results show TTFB cut by 40% when SEs pre-configure the pools.

[06:14] Priya Kapoor: Quick note — we had a small incident in late July where a config bug caused autoscale loops in a Dedicated pool. Root cause: misapplied policy in the autoscale engine; fixed and alerting improved. We retro'd and the action items are in the notes.

[06:35] Miguel Torres: Closing remarks: double down on top priorities, keep shipping. Big thanks to everyone for hitting Q2 targets. We'll circulate the deck and meeting notes.

[06:48] Ava Chen: Two housekeeping items — product AMA next Tuesday, and town hall for hiring updates the following week.

[06:56] Miguel Torres: All right, that's it. Meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hearings typical of auto-transcript (e.g., "kay-v" vs "KV"). Slides and linked docs: https://drive.redwood/all-hands/2026-08-03-deck, internal benchmark spreadsheet: https://drive.redwood/benchmarks/optimize-aug-2026
